items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: I think Dizzy, James Moody, Sonny Stitt, Wes Montgomery. I mean these are people that just were characters.

ctx.x: Right. If they had kept quiet you’d have just kept doing it.

And then eventually you fade away. So in a sense these educational things are good. We are giving a craft that students are learning a craft, but that doesn’t mean that they’re going to be great musicians. The music that — I mean you had a film of a character. Joe Williams was a character. I mean he was an entity. I mean he was something special. And © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

I think Dizzy, James Moody, Sonny Stitt, Wes Montgomery. I mean these are people that just were characters. But they had a lot of excellence. You don’t have to just be a fool. You know nobody wants to be around that. And so in a sense we are not allowing the characters to come through all this, because there’s a lot of cookie cutters now. There’s a lot of — and it’s really hard for the character to come through now, because there’s probably a little more suppressed stuff for someone who wants to go this way and…
